messages:
anya (eng-ml): quick share — ran FP8 / AWQ / GPTQ bakeoff on stable-7b in staging. short summary + a suggested packaging schema (new name to avoid qprof confusion).

matt (eng-ml): curious — what were the key numbers? latency and accuracy deltas?

anya (eng-ml): TL;DR: AWQ-int8: ~1.6x token throughput vs fp16, ppl delta +0.9%. GPTQ-8bit: throughput ~1.3x, ppl delta noisy (range -0.4% .. +0.7% across seeds). FP8 on A100: tiny latency win (~1.1x) but memory wins only on 80GB configs.

rahul (optimize): can you paste the eval table and the workloads you used? we need to map into Optimize's profile buckets.

anya (eng-ml): pasted quick table below (micro-benchmarks + eval set = mix of prompts from persona/qa/summarize):
```
model    | backend  | tput_tokens/s | ppl_delta_vs_fp16 | notes
stable-7b| fp16     | 1200          | 0.0               | baseline
stable-7b| awq-int8 | 1900          | +0.9%             | deterministic seeds
stable-7b| gptq-8   | 1560          | -0.4%..+0.7%      | high seed variance
stable-7b| fp8      | 1320          | +0.1%             | best on A100-80
```

olivia (infra): packaging question: do we intend to ship multiple artifacts per model (one per backend) or a single bundle with fallbacks? infra needs explicit hw hints for scheduler.

anya (eng-ml): propose a small new manifest called "quantkit" (keeps 'profile' ambiguous away). idea: one quantkit bundle = 1 model + 1 primary backend + optional fallback backends + eval metadata + runtime hints. lightweight, versioned.

matt (eng-ml): name sounds fine. show an example manifest.

anya (eng-ml): example manifest below (json snippet):
```json
{
  "quantkit_name": "stable-7b_awq_v1",
  "version": "2026-03-15",
  "primary_backend": "awq-int8",
  "fallbacks": ["fp16","gptq-8"],
  "hw_hints": ["a100:80gb","a10g:24gb"],
  "eval_summary": {
    "eval_commit": "c4a9f3b",
    "seed_avg_ppl_delta": "+0.9%",
    "seed_count": "5",
    "workload_tags": ["chat","summarize","qa"]
  },
  "compat_tags": ["kv-cache-v1","kv-cache-v2"],
  "optimize_channel": "fast"
}
```

rahul (optimize): two asks: 1) add an explicit numeric metric block (latency_ms, tokens/s) for Optimize to auto-suggest config; 2) add a confidence field for accuracy regressions (low/med/high).

anya (eng-ml): updated manifest locally to include metrics/confidence. also added an "eval_bench_commit" and "seed_variance_note".

ci-bot: build queued: quantkit/stable-7b_awq_v1 -> running smoke tests.

olivia (infra): also recommend a runtime_compat_id so scheduler can check kernel availability before routing. something like "rcid:awq-v1-a100".

matt (eng-ml): recommendation for Optimize channels: map to three channels so downstream teams can pick easily:
- fast = AWQ-int8 (best throughput, acceptable delta <= 1.5%)
- balanced = GPTQ-8 (moderate speed, target seed-avg delta <= 0.5% but run 3+ seeds)
- accurate = fp16 / fp8 (prioritize quality, minimal regression)

rahul (optimize): +1. we'll implement auto-routing rules in Optimize: if latency_goal < 50ms prefer fast; if quality_strict=true prefer accurate. Also will show expected token cost delta next to each quantkit.

anya (eng-ml): action items I will take: 1) open PR with quantkit schema + example manifests, 2) run 3 independent GPTQ seeds and attach seed-avg + stdev, 3) add CI lint for manifest fields and runtime_compat_id, 4) add a short doc in Optimize mapping page.

matt (eng-ml): sounds good. please tag @rahul and @olivia in the PR and add checklist.

anya (eng-ml): will do. thanks — I'll post PR number here when ready. :rocket:
